# Numerical Differentiation - Finite Differences

Numerical differentiation remains indispensable for gradient checking, validating custom backward passes, and computing gradients of black-box functions — even in an autodiff world.

## Forward Difference

$$f'(x) \approx \frac{f(x+h) - f(x)}{h}, \quad \text{error} = O(h) + O\!\left(\frac{\varepsilon_{\text{mach}}}{h}\right)$$

Optimal $h \approx \sqrt{\varepsilon_{\text{mach}}}$: ~$10^{-4}$ for fp32, ~$10^{-8}$ for fp64.

## Central Difference

$$f'(x) \approx \frac{f(x+h) - f(x-h)}{2h}, \quad \text{error} = O(h^2) + O\!\left(\frac{\varepsilon_{\text{mach}}}{h}\right)$$

Optimal $h \approx \varepsilon_{\text{mach}}^{1/3}$: ~$5\times10^{-3}$ for fp32, ~$6\times10^{-6}$ for fp64. Requires $2N$ evaluations vs $N+1$ for forward difference.

## Complex-Step Derivative

$$f'(x) \approx \frac{\operatorname{Im}[f(x+ih)]}{h}$$

No subtraction of similar numbers — no cancellation. Allows $h = 10^{-20}$ with machine-precision accuracy.

```python
import numpy as np, torch

def central_diff(f, x, h=1e-5):
    x = np.asarray(x, float); g = np.zeros_like(x)
    for i in range(len(x)):
        xp, xm = x.copy(), x.copy()
        xp[i] += h; xm[i] -= h
        g[i] = (f(xp) - f(xm)) / (2*h)
    return g

def complex_step(f, x, h=1e-20):
    x = np.asarray(x, complex); g = np.zeros(len(x))
    for i in range(len(x)):
        xc = x.copy(); xc[i] += 1j*h
        g[i] = f(xc).imag / h
    return g

f  = lambda x: np.sum(x**2)   # true grad = 2x
x0 = np.array([1., 2., 3.])
print('Analytical:  ', 2*x0)
print('Central diff:', central_diff(f, x0))   # matches
print('Complex step:', complex_step(f, x0))   # matches exactly

# PyTorch gradient checking for custom ops
func = lambda x: (x**3).sum()
x = torch.tensor([1., 2., 3.], dtype=torch.float64, requires_grad=True)
print('gradcheck:', torch.autograd.gradcheck(func, x, eps=1e-6, atol=1e-5))
```

## Step Size Selection

| Method | Truncation error | Roundoff error | Optimal h (fp64) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Forward diff | $O(h)$ | $O(\varepsilon/h)$ | ~$10^{-8}$ |
| Central diff | $O(h^2)$ | $O(\varepsilon/h)$ | ~$6\times10^{-6}$ |
| Complex step | $O(h^2)$ | none | ~$10^{-20}$ |

## Gradient Checking in Neural Networks

1. Compute analytical gradient via `backward()`.
2. For each parameter $\theta_i$: compute numerical gradient via central differences.
3. Check relative error: $|\nabla_{\text{anal}} - \nabla_{\text{num}}| / \max(|\nabla_{\text{anal}}|, |\nabla_{\text{num}}|, 10^{-8})$.
4. Pass if max relative error $< 10^{-5}$ (fp64), $< 10^{-3}$ (fp32).

Always use fp64 for gradient checking — fp32 has insufficient precision.

| Method | Error | h_opt (fp64) | Evaluations | Cancellation-free |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Forward diff | O(h) | ~1e-8 | N+1 | No |
| Central diff | O(h²) | ~6e-6 | 2N | No |
| Complex step | O(h²) | 1e-20 | N (complex) | Yes |
| Autodiff | O(ε) | N/A | 1 backward | N/A |

> **TIP: torch.autograd.gradcheck**
> `torch.autograd.gradcheck` automates gradient checking using central differences in fp64. Always run it on small inputs before trusting a custom backward implementation. Watch for: kinks at test points (ReLU at 0), non-differentiable reductions, complex input handling.

> **WARNING: Numerical Gradients Are Not a Substitute for Exact Gradients**
> Cost is $O(N)$ forward passes vs $O(1)$ for autodiff. Numerical noise corrupts gradient directions for small learning rates. Use numerical differentiation only for checking and debugging — never for training.
